Australia’s fertility rate has fallen to a record low.

Australia’s total fertility rate dropped to around 1.48 births per woman in 2025, far below the 2.1 replacement level needed to maintain population size without migration.

The rate is projected to fall further to around 1.42
The median age of mothers has reached 32
High living costs and economic pressures are contributing to delayed childbirth
The trend echoes Elon Musk’s repeated warnings about declining birth rates in developed nations

Australia’s demographic challenge is becoming increasingly difficult to ignore.

Italy’s birth rate is collapsing to historic lows.

Italy recorded just 370,000 births in 2024, the lowest level since national records began in 1861. Fertility fell to around 1.13 children per woman in early 2025 data, with the decline continuing into 2025.

Births fell further to roughly 355,000 in 2025
Fertility remained near 1.14 children per woman
Delayed parenthood, fewer women of childbearing age, and economic pressures are driving the decline
Net immigration is currently offsetting part of Italy’s natural population decrease

Italy’s demographic crisis is becoming impossible to ignore.

Elon Musk on what “Dario is right” actually meant.

"I probably should have said Dario is right."

"I did try to clarify it in subsequent posts on X, but those get much less attention."

"The danger of AI is very significant at this point."

"That we need to do better with AI safety, or we have at this point exponentially increasing risk with the AI models."

Hosts asked if he meant the harm, the regulation, or both.
He narrowed it to the risk — not a regulatory manifesto.

• Danger of AI — very significant now
• Safety bar — has to rise with the models
• Risk curve — exponentially increasing
• Clarification — X posts got less attention than the three-word stamp

Believe the people building the models when they say they are dangerous.
Peer review before release is the next move — not a slogan.

Elon Musk on why physics runs the company.

"Physics is a harsh judge."

"There's no fooling physics."

"If something's wrong, the rocket's going to explode. It's not going to get to orbit."

"Physics is the law, and everything else is a recommendation."

"I've seen people break the laws made by humans, but I've not seen anyone break the laws made by physics."

Host asked how people stay honest with him when the deadlines are intense.
Gwynne answered first — then he made it a law.

• Harsh judge — no fooling physics
• Rockets — wrong inputs explode; they don't reach orbit
• Law vs recommendation — humans break human laws; physics doesn't bend
• SpaceX culture — reality grades the homework, not the org chart

First principles is not a slogan.
It's what survives when the rocket has to fly.
